sections.h2: How can I sell a house fast in Pittsburgh?
sections.html:
Most sellers choose between an agent listing, a sale by owner and a cash offer. A listing usually brings the widest pool of buyers but depends on showings and a buyer's loan. A cash buyer can often close on a date you pick and buys the house as it stands, which matters when the roof leaks, the stairs need work or the estate wants a quick close.

Pittsburgh adds a few local steps to any of these routes. The city does not make you hold a Certificate of Occupancy to sell, the county collects the transfer tax when the deed is recorded, and the school district portion of the city tax bill follows its own collection rules. Knowing those three points up front saves a week or more at closing.

  • Confirm who is on the deed and whether any mortgage or lien must be paid from the proceeds.
  • Check the Certificate of Occupancy record on the city's online search.
  • Ask the settlement agent to total the transfer tax before you accept a price.

sections.h2: What is the transfer tax when selling in Pittsburgh?
sections.html:
A sale inside the city of Pittsburgh carries a 5% realty transfer tax in most cases: 1% to the Commonwealth, 3% to the city and 1% to the Pittsburgh School District. Allegheny County collects it for all three at the time the deed is recorded, and it is paid by a separate check from the recording fees. The county page notes that the city applied the full 5% to residential deeds recorded from February 1, 2020.

A $200,000 sale at 5% comes to $10,000. Part of the city lies in the Baldwin-Whitehall School District, where the school share is one half of one percent instead of 1%, so addresses there total 4.5%. The county's rate table lists each school district, so match your parcel to the right line before you estimate your proceeds.

Transfer tax split for a house in the city of Pittsburgh (Allegheny County Department of Real Estate)
Taxing bodyRateOn $200,000
Commonwealth of Pennsylvania1%$2,000
City of Pittsburgh3%$6,000
Pittsburgh School District1%$2,000
Total5%$10,000

The sales agreement states who pays. Transfers between close family members may need only a statement on the deed describing the relationship, while other exemptions need the state's Statement of Value form.

sections.h2: Does Pittsburgh require a Certificate of Occupancy to sell a house?
sections.html:
No. The city says it does not require a Certificate of Occupancy to sell or buy a property, unlike many municipalities around it. The city also warns that this does not mean a property meets every zoning and building code, and many older single-family homes have no certificate on file because past rules did not call for one.

A buyer may have to apply for an Occupancy Permit if the use of the building differs from the use on the latest certificate. The city tells parties to complete a Zoning Certificate request so the transaction meets Pennsylvania law. The most recent certificate is the current legal use, and two certificates can together cover a building approved in stages.

  • Search the Permits, Licenses, and Inspections online occupancy tool by address, parcel number, permit number or ward.
  • If a certificate should exist but does not appear, email the records office and expect a reply within five business days.
  • If you hold a certificate that is missing from the city's files, send a copy so it is added to the library.

sections.h2: What is it like to own and sell a home in Pittsburgh?
sections.html:
Pittsburgh sits where the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers join to form the Ohio, and the Golden Triangle of downtown points at that meeting. The Census Bureau counted 302,971 residents in 2020 and estimates 307,632 for July 2025, a gain of 1.5%. The city is divided into 90 neighborhoods, and more than a quarter of their names refer to hills, heights or similar features. That hints at the terrain: many streets are steep two-lane roads, and the city keeps about 800 sets of public stairways.

The city grew around Fort Pitt after General Forbes took the forks in 1758 and became known as the Steel City. The economy now centers on health care, education and technology, with UPMC and Allegheny Health Network as the two biggest health systems and the University of Pittsburgh and Carnegie Mellon University in the Oakland and Shadyside area. The city counts 446 bridges, more than Venice.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $205,800 (Census Bureau, 2020 to 2024).
  • Owner-occupied rate: 47.7%, so more households rent than own.
  • Median gross rent: $1,261, across 138,188 households.
  • Bachelor's degree or higher among adults 25 and older: 49.1%.
  • Average snowfall runs about 44 inches a year.

sections.h2: How do Pittsburgh and Allegheny County property taxes work for a seller?
sections.html:
The city, the parks fund, the Carnegie Library and the Pittsburgh School District all bill on the value set by the Allegheny County Office of Property Assessments. County values follow a base year of 2012, so the assessed figure is not a current market price. Bills go out in January, the gross amount is due the last day of February, and a 2% discount applies for early payment. Installments fall at the end of February, April and July.

If you owe tax from earlier years, the city keeps past-due city, library and parks tax, while past-due school tax sits with Jordan Tax Service, Inc. An unpaid balance can lead to a Treasurer's Sale. Ask the Department of Finance and the collector for payoff figures before closing, since both come out of the proceeds.

The homestead program reduces the taxable value of an owner-occupied home. The city's reduction is $15,000, worth $120.90 a year in city tax, and a county homestead application also activates the city, school and library exemptions. A buyer who will live in the house should apply through the county. Assessment appeals follow an annual window: for tax year 2027 it ran from July 1 to September 1, 2026 and has closed, Check the county's real estate portal for the dates of the next window.

sections.h2: What disclosures must a Pittsburgh seller make?
sections.html:
Pennsylvania's Real Estate Seller Disclosure Law requires a seller to hand the buyer a signed and dated property disclosure statement before both sides sign the agreement of transfer. The form covers the roof, basement, structure, additions, water and sewer, plumbing, wiring, heating, land and drainage including sinkholes and flood risk indicators, hazardous substances, title issues and storm water facilities. On a hillside lot, the land and drainage items deserve extra attention.

A seller does not have to investigate the property but must not state anything known to be false. If the facts change before settlement, the seller must tell the buyer. A condominium seller discloses only about the unit, and a fiduciary selling for an estate is outside the chapter.

sections.h2: What should I check before accepting an offer on a Pittsburgh house?
sections.html:
Match the offer to your real net. Subtract the 5% or 4.5% transfer tax if you are paying it, the recording fees, any payoff and unpaid tax, and the cost of repairs the buyer expects you to make. Then compare that figure across a listing, a sale by owner and a cash offer.

  • Is the property inside the city or in a neighboring borough with a lower rate?
  • Does the Certificate of Occupancy record match how the house is used today?
  • Are city, library, parks and school tax paid through the current installment?
  • Who is named on the deed, and is probate or a payoff needed first?

faqs.q: Do I need a Certificate of Occupancy to sell in Pittsburgh?
faqs.a: No, the city does not require one for a sale. A buyer may still have to apply for an Occupancy Permit if the use differs from the last certificate, and the city asks parties to file a Zoning Certificate request. Search the online occupancy tool or email the records office to see what is on file.

faqs.q: How much is the Pittsburgh transfer tax?
faqs.a: It is 5% for most city sales: 1% state, 3% city and 1% school district. Properties in the Baldwin-Whitehall School District part of the city pay a half-percent school share, which makes 4.5%. Allegheny County collects the tax when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: When are Pittsburgh real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: The gross amount is due the last day of February, with installments due the last day of February, April and July. A 2% discount is available for early payment. Ask the city's Department of Finance for the exact discount date on your bill.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Allegheny County assessment this year?
faqs.a: No. The window for tax year 2027 ran from July 1 to September 1, 2026 and is closed. Check the county's real estate portal for the next window if you think the value is wrong.

faqs.q: What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: It ends with the sale, and the buyer applies for their own. The city homestead reduction is $15,000, and a county homestead application also triggers the city, school district and library exemptions for an owner who lives in the house.
